inputs: Account-level ownership and payment history
State limitation, revival, and collection-disclosure matrix
Dispute records and credit-reporting eligibility dates
workflow: 1. Validate account ownership, balances, bankruptcy status, and applicable limitation periods
2. Obtain licensed legal review of collectibility, required notices, and payment-revival consequences
3. Offer permitted voluntary self-service resolutions without lawsuit threats or credit-deletion promises
4. Honor disputes and opt-outs, issue satisfaction records, and update only accurate eligible reporting
metrics: Validated legally collectible balance share
Net voluntary receipts after servicing costs
Dispute and disclosure-defect rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Time-barred collection or reporting violation
platform_risks.trigger: Threatened litigation, unlawful revival solicitation, or re-aging of obsolete debt
platform_risks.impact: Enforcement, restitution, and servicing suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Accounts failing legal-age checks and substantiated complaints
platform_risks.fallback: Suppress affected accounts, correct reporting, and suspend collection until counsel approves remediation

plays.name: Aged Shelf-Corp Reinstatement, Primary Tradeline & 0%-APR Corporate Credit Stacking
plays.mechanism: Compare reinstated entities and genuine business credit facilities for working-capital financing; entity age is not operating history, and promotional APR economics require accurate underwriting and repayment capacity.
inputs: Entity filings, beneficial ownership, and liability searches
Verified operating financials and genuine supplier tradelines
Lender eligibility, promotional APR, fee, and guarantee terms
workflow: 1. Audit the entity's ownership, tax liabilities, and reinstatement requirements
2. Disclose acquisition and actual operating history; establish only genuine paid supplier accounts
3. Compare lender-approved applications with full debt disclosure and consolidated exposure limits
4. Fund documented business expenses and repay before promotional expiry using cash-flow reserves
metrics: Effective borrowing cost including fees
Debt service coverage under post-promotion APR
Utilization and days to promotional expiry

platform_risks.failure_mode: Credit withdrawal or unaffordable repricing
platform_risks.trigger: Misstated operating history, undisclosed debt, or expired promotional terms
platform_risks.impact: Account closure, accelerated repayment, and guarantee exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Underwriting discrepancies and stressed repayment coverage
platform_risks.fallback: Halt applications, correct disclosures, and use a transparent term facility or reduce financed spending

plays.name: Cell-Tower, Rooftop & Billboard Perpetual Easement Strip-Out Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Separate assignable site-access and rent rights from underlying real estate for specialist buyers, pricing tenant termination rights and the permanent burden left on the residual property.
inputs: Tower, rooftop, and billboard leases and amendments
Title, lender consent, and zoning documents
Specialist easement-buyer bids and residual property appraisals
workflow: 1. Identify leased sites and reconcile actual rent receipts with termination and renewal terms
2. Verify assignment rights, mortgage restrictions, maintenance duties, and required consents
3. Compare easement sale proceeds against lost rent and residual property impairment
4. Close approved conveyances through escrow and record access, utilities, and rent-allocation rights
metrics: Net easement proceeds versus retained rent value
Residual property value impairment
Consent-to-close cycle days

platform_risks.failure_mode: Nonassignable lease or excessive permanent property burden
platform_risks.trigger: Missing tenant or lender consent or easement scope exceeding valued rights
platform_risks.impact: Failed closing or reduced refinancing and resale value
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved consent conditions and residual appraisal discount
platform_risks.fallback: Retain the lease or negotiate a narrower term-limited assignment with all required approvals

plays.name: MCA UCC-1 Trigger Stacking & Dual-Sided Default-Restructure Brokerage
plays.mechanism: Use UCC filing changes to identify businesses that may need cash-flow review and consensual MCA restructuring, with verified obligations and disclosed compensation rather than encouraging undisclosed stacking.
inputs: Public UCC filings and termination records
Merchant-authorized contracts and cash-flow statements
Broker licensing rules and disclosed creditor compensation terms
workflow: 1. Treat UCC changes as outreach signals, not proof of default, and obtain merchant authorization
2. Reconcile advances, liens, repayment pulls, covenants, and sustainable payment capacity
3. Disclose dual-sided fees and conflicts; use independent counsel where representation would conflict
4. Coordinate documented creditor-approved modifications and monitor actual payment relief
metrics: Net merchant payment relief after fees
Creditor-approved modification rate
Post-restructure missed-payment rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Conflicted brokerage or prohibited stacking worsens default
platform_risks.trigger: Hidden commissions, inaccurate balances, or new financing breaching existing contracts
platform_risks.impact: Accelerated collections and broker liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: Undisclosed fee exceptions and covenant breaches per engagement
platform_risks.fallback: Stop placement, refund improper fees, and refer the merchant to independent licensed restructuring counsel

plays.name: Whitelisted Agency Ad-Spend Card-Multiplier Points & Volume-Rebate Cycling
plays.mechanism: Route genuine client-authorized advertising spend through eligible agency payment arrangements to earn contract-permitted rewards and volume rebates, net of financing, processing, and client pass-through obligations.
inputs: Client media mandates and rebate ownership clauses
Issuer reward categories, caps, and repayment terms
Platform invoices and agency volume-rebate agreements
workflow: 1. Verify client authorization, platform payment permissions, and ownership of rewards and rebates
2. Model eligible media purchases against reward caps, fees, liquidity, and rebate thresholds
3. Pay only genuine approved advertising invoices without circular spend or fabricated transactions
4. Reconcile settled rewards, client credits, refunds, and full card repayment each statement cycle
metrics: Net retained rewards and rebates per media dollar
Unfunded client exposure and repayment coverage
Invoice-to-reward reconciliation variance

platform_risks.failure_mode: Reward clawback or client-funded liquidity shortfall
platform_risks.trigger: Ineligible categories, prohibited payment aggregation, or delayed client reimbursement
platform_risks.impact: Lost rebates, interest costs, and card suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Denied reward value and overdue client balances versus cash reserves
platform_risks.fallback: Move to client-direct billing or prefunded approved agency terms and stop rewards-dependent spending

plays.name: IRC Section 179D Government & Nonprofit Energy-Deduction Allocation Brokering
plays.mechanism: Coordinate eligible government and tax-exempt building owners, qualifying designers, and independent energy certifiers to document Section 179D deduction allocations; compensation is for permitted services, not resale of a freely transferable deduction.
inputs: Public and nonprofit building project records and construction dates
Designer contracts and owner allocation authority
Independent energy certification and applicable tax-year eligibility rules
workflow: 1. Screen building projects for eligible ownership, construction timing, and current Section 179D availability
2. Verify qualifying designer work, energy certification, deduction limits, and applicable wage and apprenticeship requirements
3. Obtain authorized owner allocation letters and reconcile prior allocations to prevent duplicate deductions
4. Deliver the substantiated file to the designer's tax adviser and collect disclosed legally permitted coordination fees
metrics: Certified eligible deduction value allocated
Owner-approved allocation conversion rate
Net coordination fees after certification and review costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Deduction allocation rejected or reduced
platform_risks.trigger: Ineligible project dates, unsupported designer status, deficient certification, or duplicate allocation
platform_risks.impact: Lost tax benefit, assessment exposure, and disputed service fees
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved eligibility and allocation exceptions per project
platform_risks.fallback: Pause allocation, obtain independent tax review, and offer fixed-fee documentation support only for eligible projects

plays.name: Automated Form 8850 WOTC (Work Opportunity Tax Credit) & Section 41 R&D Contingency Engine
plays.mechanism: Automate employer-authorized WOTC screening and separately substantiate Section 41 research credits, earning outcome-linked service fees only where permitted; program authorization, qualifying activities, wage coordination, and professional fee restrictions govern each claim.
inputs: Consented hiring records, Form 8850 responses, and payroll hours
Research project evidence and qualified expense ledgers
State workforce certification procedures and tax-year credit and fee rules
workflow: 1. Confirm WOTC authorization for each hire date and complete required prescreening by the job-offer date
2. Submit Form 8850 and required supporting forms within the applicable 28-day deadline and track state certification and qualifying hours
3. Separately document Section 41 qualifying research and expenses, reconciling wage overlap and applicable deduction adjustments with a tax professional
4. Obtain employer and preparer approval before filing, retain audit support, and collect permitted fees without guaranteeing credits
metrics: Timely WOTC certification submission rate
Substantiated credits realized by the employer
Net permitted service fees after review and filing costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Credit denial or impermissible contingent-fee arrangement
platform_risks.trigger: Expired program authority, late certification, unsupported research expenses, or restricted practitioner compensation
platform_risks.impact: Reduced credits, amended returns, penalties, and fee repayment exposure
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deadline exceptions, certification denials, and unsupported expense share
platform_risks.fallback: Exclude unsupported claims and use compliant fixed-fee payroll and research-documentation services under independent tax review

plays.name: State Film, Historic Rehabilitation (HTC) & Brownfield Transferable Tax Credit Placement
plays.mechanism: Match certified state film, historic rehabilitation, and brownfield credits with eligible taxpayers at negotiated discounts, retaining disclosed placement fees; transferability and buyer usability are state-specific and do not imply federal historic credits can be sold outright.
inputs: State agency project approvals and issued credit certificates
Transfer rules, recapture terms, and seller ownership records
Buyer state tax liabilities and escrow placement agreements
workflow: 1. Identify certified credits and verify state-specific transferability, issuance status, and remaining carryforward life
2. Have independent advisers validate eligible costs, ownership, liens, recapture exposure, and buyer utilization limits
3. Match approved buyers and sellers with disclosed pricing, fees, indemnities, and any available insurance exclusions
4. Complete required agency transfer approvals and escrow settlement, then retain filing and post-close monitoring records
metrics: Certified transferable credit face value placed
Net placement fee per settled transaction
Transfer approval and escrow cycle days

platform_risks.failure_mode: Transfer rejected or purchased credit unusable
platform_risks.trigger: State rule change, certificate defect, recapture event, or buyer liability mismatch
platform_risks.impact: Failed closing or buyer tax shortfall and indemnity dispute
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved certificate exceptions and buyer utilization coverage
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend settlement under diligence contingencies and rematch only verified eligible credits without guaranteeing tax savings

plays.name: Commercial Solar Tax-Equity Flip & Bonus-Depreciation Strip Syndication
plays.mechanism: Arrange commercial solar partnership-flip investments that allocate supported tax benefits and cash flows to genuine equity owners; depreciation cannot be sold as a standalone credit, and allocations require economic substance, tax compliance, and securities-law review.
inputs: Solar project costs, ownership records, and operating contracts
Investor tax capacity and dated depreciation eligibility analysis
Counsel-reviewed partnership waterfall and securities offering documents
workflow: 1. Underwrite project cash flows, eligible basis, construction and service dates, and current credit and depreciation availability
2. Verify investor suitability, tax capacity, at-risk and passive-loss limits, and applicable securities and intermediary requirements
3. Structure counsel-approved partnership allocations and flip terms with genuine equity risk, basis adjustments, and recapture protections
4. Close through authorized intermediaries and monitor operations, tax reporting, and flip conditions before distributing permitted fees
metrics: Qualified tax-equity capital closed
Realized investor distributions versus underwritten waterfall
Net permitted placement fees after legal and diligence costs

candidates.title: Judgment Recovery
candidates.uncertainty_note: Editorial sensitivity band, not a statistical interval. Confidence is a supplied classification; independent source review is required.

score_rationale.revenue_potential: Revenue Potential: 20/25. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.
score_rationale.profit_margin_potential: Profit Margin Potential: 21/25. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.
score_rationale.team_efficiency: Team Efficiency: 16/20. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.
score_rationale.startup_accessibility: Startup Accessibility: 10/15. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.
score_rationale.automation_potential: Automation Potential: 10/15. Contingent collections can be efficient but many judgments are uncollectible.

economics.owner_net_profit_potential: $12,000–$200,000 USD annually, before personal taxes and reinvestment
economics.includes_contractors_note: Headcount includes the working owner and recurring contractors as people, not FTE equivalents. Contractors may be part-time. Scaled scenario adds one employee and one contractor; external vendor workforces are not counted as internal team members.
economics.revenue_basis: Recognized service fees, not client asset value
economics.cost_basis: Annual net margins include operating expenses and non-owner labor; monthly opex is fixed/semi-fixed overhead only. No owner salary is deducted. Capital needs may grow beyond startup range.
economics.estimate_status: Illustrative assumptions; not verified earnings data

conservative.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

base_case.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

scaled_small_team.assumption: Illustrative established-operation run rate, not first-year earnings. Margin includes operating costs and non-owner labor; owner labor is not separately compensated. Scale requires additional demand, working capital and delivery capacity.

regulatory_notes: Check collection licensing, consumer-debt rules, exemptions and lawful data access.

plays.name: Public-Record & API Intelligence
plays.mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.
inputs: Court & probate dockets
State controller ledgers
Public licensing & entity APIs
workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence
Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold
Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution
metrics: Cost per verified lead
Docket-to-contact latency (hours)
Net recovery / conversion rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating
platform_risks.trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals
platform_risks.impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry
platform_risks.detection_metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta
platform_risks.fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues

plays.name: Distressed Asset Recovery
plays.mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.
inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers
Unclaimed property & judgment dockets
Surplus auction manifests
workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances
Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value
Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts
metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case
Claim approval rate
Days from filing to disbursement

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold
platform_risks.trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules
platform_risks.impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle
platform_risks.detection_metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance
platform_risks.fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required

plays.name: B2B Class-Action & Antitrust Settlement Contingency Recovery
plays.mechanism: Monitor multibillion-dollar corporate antitrust and commercial class-action settlement funds (payment-card interchange, freight, auto parts, commercial insurance, SaaS) where 85–90% of eligible small businesses never file, and recover verified payouts on a 25–33% contingency fee.
inputs: Active federal B2B class-action settlement docket calendar & claims-administrator portals
B2B merchant-processing, fleet, & vendor spend intake pipeline
Contingency claim-preparation & court-authorized third-party filing agreements
workflow: Track open and upcoming commercial class-action settlements with verified court-appointed claims administrators and $50M–$5B+ settlement pools
Sign zero-upfront-cost (25–33% contingency) authorization agreements with operating restaurants, medical practices, retailers, and fleets
Extract historical merchant statements or vendor invoices, submit audited claim packages to the settlement administrator, and reconcile fee splits upon disbursement
metrics: Average gross settlement recovery per enrolled business ($5,000–$150,000+)
Claim acceptance rate by court-appointed administrator (%)
Net contingency fee per operator hour invested

platform_risks.failure_mode: Claim rejection, administrator audit hold, or court cap on third-party filer fees
platform_risks.trigger: Submitting unsubstantiated spend estimates, missing court bar dates, or failing to include required third-party filer disclosures
platform_risks.impact: Delayed payout disbursement or court-mandated fee reduction
platform_risks.detection_metric: Deficiency-notice rate (<2% target) and 100% court-approved disclosure compliance
platform_risks.fallback: File strictly for verified operating businesses with primary processor/vendor statements and use court-approved third-party claim-filing riders

plays.name: Arizona ABS Law-Firm Ownership & Survivor/Mass-Tort Co-Counsel Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Leverage Arizona Supreme Court Rule 31.1(c) and ACJA § 7-209 (which abolished ABA Rule 5.4 in Arizona via Alternative Business Structure [ABS] licensing) so non-lawyer acquisition operators can legally own an Arizona law firm, acquire inbound institutional sexual assault survivor claims (juvenile detention facilities, rideshare MDLs, clergy/boarding-school/medical lookback windows) and catastrophic mass torts, and participate in lawful co-counsel contingency fee splits ($50k–$400k+ per settled case) instead of capped flat marketing fees.
inputs: Arizona Supreme Court ABS license + designated Compliance Lawyer (ACJA § 7-209)
Trauma-informed inbound acquisition funnels for state sexual-assault lookback windows & federal MDLs
24/7 HIPAA-compliant survivor intake, facility/ride-receipt verification, & national trial co-counsel network
workflow: Form or partner with a licensed Arizona ABS law firm with an appointed Arizona-bar Compliance Lawyer to legally bridge digital acquisition and legal representation
Run empathetic, 100% inbound survivor-advocacy campaigns across open statutory lookback windows (juvenile detention centers, Uber/Lyft rideshare MDL 3084, institutional/youth-facility abuse)

Execute trauma-informed intake, verify facility/detention/rideshare records, and co-counsel with specialized trial litigators under Rule 1.5(e) joint-responsibility agreements to share in back-end settlement fees
metrics: Cost per signed & record-verified survivor retainer ($1,200–$3,500 media cost)
Facility/rideshare corroboration pass rate (%) & zero-fraud docket quality
Realized co-counsel contingency fee per settled case ($50,000–$400,000+ vs. $3k lead sale)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Cross-jurisdictional Rule 5.4 fee-splitting challenges, MDL claimant-fraud rejections, or 24–48 month settlement lockup
platform_risks.trigger: Splitting fees in non-ABS jurisdictions without genuine legal services/joint responsibility by ABS attorneys, accepting unverified lead-brokered retainers, or undercapitalizing multi-year MDL hold times
platform_risks.impact: Disallowance of co-counsel fee division in restrictive states, court dismissal of uncorroborated claims, or working-capital exhaustion before settlement payout
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% primary-record corroboration rate (detention/medical/ride logs) and state-by-state Rule 1.5(e)/5.4 ethics opinion sign-off
platform_risks.fallback: Ensure licensed ABS attorneys perform substantive legal intake/case-work or pair with an MSO (Management Services Organization) structure in restrictive states, enforce strict primary-document verification before filing, and blend fast-settling single-event injury cases with multi-year institutional dockets

plays.name: State Treasury Escheatment & Unclaimed Corporate Warrant Recovery
plays.mechanism: Ingest state controller/treasury escheatment ledgers and uncashed municipal/corporate warrant registries above $25,000, cross-match corporate officers via Secretary of State filings, and execute statutory recovery agreements for a 10–25% contingent finder fee.
inputs: State controller/treasury escheatment bulk ledgers
Uncashed municipal warrant & vendor-credit registries
Secretary of State officer & FEIN cross-match index
workflow: Filter state unclaimed-property and uncashed-warrant ledgers for high-value corporate and estate accounts exceeding $25,000
Resolve active corporate officers, successor entities, or authorized fiduciaries via SOS and skip-trace databases
Execute state-compliant finder agreements with statutory fee caps and submit notarized claim packages to the treasury administrator
metrics: Average gross warrant/escheatment claim size ($25k+)
Treasury claim approval rate (%)
Days from notarized filing to state disbursement

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory finder-fee cap violation or waiting-period rejection
platform_risks.trigger: Charging above state statutory fee limits (e.g., 10% in CA/FL/NY) or soliciting claims during restricted post-escheatment windows
platform_risks.impact: Voided recovery contract, state controller rejection, or administrative penalty
platform_risks.detection_metric: State-by-state fee-cap compliance check (100% pass) and claim rejection notice rate
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce per-state statutory fee caps and waiting-period rules in intake templates and disclose the owner's right to claim directly for free

plays.name: UCC-1 Filing, MCA Stacking & Maturity-Date Trigger Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Monitor state Secretary of State UCC-1 financing statements and continuation filings to identify operating businesses 4–9 months into high-cost Merchant Cash Advances (MCAs) or equipment notes, triggering refinance and debt-consolidation live transfers.
inputs: Daily state SOS UCC-1 initial, amendment, & termination bulk feeds
Secured-party lender dictionary (identifying MCA vs. bank/SBA filings)
Live-transfer commercial refinance & SBA consolidation desk
workflow: Classify daily UCC-1 filings by secured party to isolate businesses that took high-cost short-term working capital 120–240 days ago
Enrich business owner direct phone and email and score by industry revenue stability
Contact merchants during peak renewal/payoff windows to offer lower-rate term consolidation or equipment refinancing, monetizing via broker points or live-transfer fees
metrics: UCC-to-verified-decision-maker match rate (%)
Live-transfer qualification rate (%)
Origination commission / referral fee per funded refi

platform_risks.failure_mode: TCPA automated-calling liability or state commercial-financing disclosure violations
platform_risks.trigger: Robocalling cell phones without consent or quoting misleading APRs in states with commercial Truth-in-Lending laws (CA, NY, UT, VA)
platform_risks.impact: Statutory TCPA demand letters or state DFPI regulatory enforcement
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% DNC/litigator-scrub pass rate and statutory APR disclosure audit in regulated states
platform_risks.fallback: Use direct mail, B2B work-email sequences, and manual human-dialed outreach paired with compliant state commercial financing disclosures

plays.name: Out-of-Network Medical Claim & ERISA Appeal Contingency Recovery
plays.mechanism: Partner with surgical centers, air/ground ambulance operators, and specialty clinics to ingest underpaid or denied commercial insurance claims, automating federal No Surprises Act IDR (Independent Dispute Resolution) and ERISA administrative appeals on a 20–35% contingency fee.
inputs: Provider 835/837 EDI remittance & denial feeds (CO-45, CO-50, PR-96 codes)
Qualified Payment Amount (QPA) & regional FAIR Health benchmark database
Automated ERISA plan-document demand & Federal IDR portal filing workflow
workflow: Ingest denied and severely underpaid out-of-network commercial claims from specialty medical practices
Cross-reference payer remittances against statutory Open Negotiation windows (30 business days) under the No Surprises Act and ERISA SPD timelines
Generate evidence-backed arbitration briefs and ERISA appeals, collecting 20–35% of the incremental insurer payout above the initial remittance
metrics: Average incremental recovery per arbitrated claim ($1,500–$25,000+)
IDR / ERISA appeal win rate vs. initial payer offer (%)
Contingency revenue per practice partner per month

platform_risks.failure_mode: Missed 30-day Open Negotiation / 4-day IDR initiation statutory deadlines or HIPAA breach
platform_risks.trigger: Failing to file within strict federal No Surprises Act business-day windows or handling PHI without a signed Business Associate Agreement (BAA)
platform_risks.impact: Permanent forfeiture of IDR arbitration eligibility on expired claims or HIPAA compliance penalties
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% BAA execution before EDI ingestion and automated T-minus-5-day statutory deadline alerts
platform_risks.fallback: Enforce HIPAA-compliant encrypted EDI pipelines with signed BAAs and fall back to longer-window ERISA administrative appeals when IDR windows have lapsed

plays.name: Transferable Federal & State Tax Credit Brokerage & Syndication (IRA § 6418 / Film / Historic)
plays.mechanism: Scraping federal DOE/EPA interconnection queues, state film offices, and historic-preservation registries to originate transferable tax credits (IRC § 6418 Clean Energy Investment/Production Credits, Georgia/Louisiana Film Credits, State Historic Rehab & Brownfield Credits) from cash-strapped project developers at $0.82–$0.88 on the dollar and flipping them in simultaneous escrow closings to corporate and HNW taxpayers at $0.92–$0.96 on the dollar.
inputs: State film-office production certifications, National Park Service Part 2/3 Historic Preservation filings, and utility solar/biogas/storage interconnection queues
IRS Energy Credits Online pre-filing registration verification and tax-credit recapture insurance underwriting partners
Outbound network of CPA managing partners, corporate tax directors, and family-office CIOs with $1M–$50M+ in quarterly federal/state tax liabilities
workflow: Monitor public project registries to identify middle-market solar, RNG, battery storage, independent film, and historic-rehab developers holding $1M–$25M in newly generated transferable credits
Lock up exclusive purchase or placement options at $0.83–$0.89 per $1.00 of credit prior to quarterly corporate estimated tax deadlines (April 15, June 15, Sept 15, Dec 15)
Package the credits with a third-party CPA cost-segregation/eligibility opinion and tax-credit recapture insurance policy

Execute a simultaneous bilateral escrow closing with a corporate taxpayer at $0.92–$0.95 on the dollar—saving the buyer 5–8% guaranteed on their tax bill while capturing a 400–800 bps riskless spread ($40k–$80k per $1M block)
metrics: Face value of tax credits placed per quarter ($5M–$100M+)
Net retained principal/brokerage spread (400–800 bps) per closed tranche
Days in escrow from developer IRS registration number issuance to wire settlement

platform_risks.failure_mode: IRS § 6418 recapture event or state department-of-revenue basis challenge
platform_risks.trigger: Project developer inflating eligible cost basis or taking a clean-energy asset out of service during the 5-year recapture window
platform_risks.impact: Taxpayer recapture assessment plus penalties if uninsured
platform_risks.detection_metric: 100% independent Big-4/national CPA cost-basis audit and mandatory A-rated tax-credit recapture insurance binder on every tranche
platform_risks.fallback: Never take unhedged balance-sheet inventory risk; close strictly via simultaneous back-to-back escrow funded by the buyer's wire and backed by non-cancelable tax-credit insurance

plays.name: Litigation-Finance Mass-Tort Lead-to-Docket Securitization & Co-Counsel Syndicates
plays.mechanism: Pairing an Arizona Alternative Business Structure (ABS) or co-counsel law firm with an institutional litigation-finance credit facility to acquire, medically verify (via $6.50 HITECH patient-directed record requests), and package 1,000–25,000 retained mass-tort plaintiffs (PFAS, AFFF, Paraquat, NEC, rideshare assault, defective medical devices) at $1,200–$2,500 CAC—either flipping vetted case tranches to litigation-finance hedge funds at 2.5x–4x cost or holding for 35–40% global MDL settlement fee splits.
inputs: Judicial Panel on Multidistrict Litigation (JPML) docket analytics, FDA FAERS adverse-event spikes, and EPA contaminant zip-code maps
Arizona ABS / co-counsel retainer infrastructure with e-sign intake and automated HITECH Act (45 CFR § 164.524) medical-record retrieval engine
Non-recourse litigation-finance warehouse credit facility and MDL leadership co-counsel placement contracts
workflow: Identify emerging MDL mass torts with clear causation biomarkers (specific ICD-10 diagnosis codes + geographic/product exposure proof) and deep-pocket corporate defendants
Run hyper-targeted CTV, paid social, and public-record outbound campaigns to sign injured claimants directly onto joint co-counsel retainer agreements

Execute automated HITECH patient-directed electronic medical record (EMR) pulls at the federal statutory cap (~$6.50/record) and use LLM clinical parsers to verify qualifying diagnosis and exposure dates within 72 hours

Securitize verified, deficiency-free case tranches into litigation-finance buyout facilities at $4,500–$9,000 per vetted retainer or hold on the balance sheet for $25,000–$80,000+ gross contingency fees at MDL settlement
metrics: All-in cost per medically verified, deficiency-free retained plaintiff ($1,200–$2,500)
HITECH medical-record retrieval turnaround time (hours) and clinical qualification pass rate (%)
Secondary docket tranche sale multiple (2.5x–4.0x CAC) or net MDL settlement IRR

platform_risks.failure_mode: Daubert general-causation dismissal in the MDL or fraudulent duplicate claimant intake
platform_risks.trigger: Federal MDL judge excluding plaintiff expert witnesses under Rule 702 or lead vendors submitting synthetic/dual-represented claimants
platform_risks.impact: Write-down of single-tort docket value or MDL leadership rejecting duplicate retainers
platform_risks.detection_metric: Real-time SSN/lexis duplicate-retainer cross-check, immediate HITECH EMR verification before media payout, and max 20% capital concentration in any single MDL
platform_risks.fallback: Diversify docket holdings across 6–10 uncorrelated mass torts and single-event commercial casualty niches, pay media vendors strictly on EMR-verified retainers, and offload 50% of tranche cost basis early to institutional litigation funders

plays.name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Price small HOA priority liens and tax-sale interests using jurisdiction-specific priority, notice, and redemption rules; returns depend on enforceable rights, not assumed title extinguishment.
inputs: County tax-sale and HOA lien records
Title report and statutory redemption calendar
Local counsel priority and notice opinion
workflow: 1. Screen small-balance liens against property value, senior debt, and sale eligibility
2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions
3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline
4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire
metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs
Capital days outstanding
Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien
platform_risks.trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority
platform_risks.impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests

plays.name: CIPA Wiretap-Pixel & VPPA Statutory Privacy-Demand Settlement Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Support counsel-led evaluation of genuine tracking-related privacy claims using preserved consent and disclosure evidence; applicability, standing, and recoverable damages require individual legal review.
inputs: Client-authorized browser network captures
Timestamped consent flows and privacy notices
Counsel-reviewed standing and statutory applicability checklist
workflow: 1. Obtain client authorization and preserve ordinary-session tracking and consent evidence
2. Have counsel assess actual disclosures, statutory coverage, standing, and limitation periods
3. Route substantiated matters to retained counsel for proportionate notice and resolution
4. Record outcomes, client distributions, and remediation without duplicate or fabricated claims
metrics: Counsel-validated matters per reviewed session
Net client recovery after disclosed costs
Evidence completeness and duplicate-claim rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Unsupported statutory demand or evidence rejection
platform_risks.trigger: Missing standing, valid consent, or unreliable attribution of disclosed data
platform_risks.impact: Dismissal, sanctions exposure, and wasted case costs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Counsel rejection rate by coverage and evidence defect
platform_risks.fallback: Close unsupported matters and offer authorized privacy-remediation audits instead

plays.name: Chapter 11 Bankruptcy Schedule E/F Trade-Claim & Convenience-Class Rollups
plays.mechanism: Purchase documented small trade claims below risk-adjusted expected plan distributions, accounting for objections, assignment procedures, and plan rules that may prohibit claim splitting or aggregation benefits.
inputs: Bankruptcy schedules E/F and claims register
Invoices, payment history, and assignment documents
Proposed plan classification and distribution waterfall
workflow: 1. Reconcile scheduled trade creditors with filed claims and supporting invoices
2. Model recoveries under plan amendments, objections, setoffs, and convenience-class eligibility
3. Buy eligible claims through documented assignments and complete required transfer notices
4. Monitor objections and confirmation, then reconcile distributions to each acquired claim
metrics: Purchase discount to risk-adjusted recovery
Allowed claim value versus purchased face value
Realized return and days to distribution

platform_risks.failure_mode: Claim disallowance or convenience-class exclusion
platform_risks.trigger: Disputed invoices, setoff rights, or plan restrictions on purchased or split claims
platform_risks.impact: Reduced distribution or complete capital loss
platform_risks.detection_metric: Objection rate and eligible allowed value per portfolio
platform_risks.fallback: Stop affected purchases, enforce documented seller recourse where available, and price only supported general-unsecured recoveries

plays.name: Out-of-Statute Charged-Off Debt Portfolio & Self-Serve Tradeline Settlement Funnels
plays.mechanism: Evaluate heavily discounted time-barred receivables for lawful voluntary resolution, separating collection limitation periods from credit-reporting limits and excluding extinguished or otherwise uncollectible obligations.
inputs: Account-level ownership and payment history
State limitation, revival, and collection-disclosure matrix
Dispute records and credit-reporting eligibility dates
workflow: 1. Validate account ownership, balances, bankruptcy status, and applicable limitation periods
2. Obtain licensed legal review of collectibility, required notices, and payment-revival consequences
3. Offer permitted voluntary self-service resolutions without lawsuit threats or credit-deletion promises
4. Honor disputes and opt-outs, issue satisfaction records, and update only accurate eligible reporting
metrics: Validated legally collectible balance share
Net voluntary receipts after servicing costs
Dispute and disclosure-defect rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Time-barred collection or reporting violation
platform_risks.trigger: Threatened litigation, unlawful revival solicitation, or re-aging of obsolete debt
platform_risks.impact: Enforcement, restitution, and servicing suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Accounts failing legal-age checks and substantiated complaints
platform_risks.fallback: Suppress affected accounts, correct reporting, and suspend collection until counsel approves remediation

plays.name: MCA UCC-1 Trigger Stacking & Dual-Sided Default-Restructure Brokerage
plays.mechanism: Use UCC filing changes to identify businesses that may need cash-flow review and consensual MCA restructuring, with verified obligations and disclosed compensation rather than encouraging undisclosed stacking.
inputs: Public UCC filings and termination records
Merchant-authorized contracts and cash-flow statements
Broker licensing rules and disclosed creditor compensation terms
workflow: 1. Treat UCC changes as outreach signals, not proof of default, and obtain merchant authorization
2. Reconcile advances, liens, repayment pulls, covenants, and sustainable payment capacity
3. Disclose dual-sided fees and conflicts; use independent counsel where representation would conflict
4. Coordinate documented creditor-approved modifications and monitor actual payment relief
metrics: Net merchant payment relief after fees
Creditor-approved modification rate
Post-restructure missed-payment rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Conflicted brokerage or prohibited stacking worsens default
platform_risks.trigger: Hidden commissions, inaccurate balances, or new financing breaching existing contracts
platform_risks.impact: Accelerated collections and broker liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: Undisclosed fee exceptions and covenant breaches per engagement
platform_risks.fallback: Stop placement, refund improper fees, and refer the merchant to independent licensed restructuring counsel

plays.name: State Film, Historic Rehabilitation (HTC) & Brownfield Transferable Tax Credit Placement
plays.mechanism: Match certified state film, historic rehabilitation, and brownfield credits with eligible taxpayers at negotiated discounts, retaining disclosed placement fees; transferability and buyer usability are state-specific and do not imply federal historic credits can be sold outright.
inputs: State agency project approvals and issued credit certificates
Transfer rules, recapture terms, and seller ownership records
Buyer state tax liabilities and escrow placement agreements
workflow: 1. Identify certified credits and verify state-specific transferability, issuance status, and remaining carryforward life
2. Have independent advisers validate eligible costs, ownership, liens, recapture exposure, and buyer utilization limits
3. Match approved buyers and sellers with disclosed pricing, fees, indemnities, and any available insurance exclusions
4. Complete required agency transfer approvals and escrow settlement, then retain filing and post-close monitoring records
metrics: Certified transferable credit face value placed
Net placement fee per settled transaction
Transfer approval and escrow cycle days

inputs: Court & probate dockets
State controller ledgers
Public licensing & entity APIs
workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence
Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold
Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution
metrics: Cost per verified lead
Docket-to-contact latency (hours)
Net recovery / conversion rate

plays.name: New-LLC & Recorded-Deed Trigger-Mail Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Ingest daily Secretary of State new-LLC filings and County Recorder new-deed/mortgage recordings to trigger programmatic direct mail via API—replacing illegal government-lookalike poster/deed invoices (which violate 39 U.S.C. § 3001 and state deed-solicitation laws) with high-LTV recurring workplace compliance subscriptions, property-tax appeal contingency offers, and exclusive new-mover/B2B lead monetization.
inputs: Daily Secretary of State new-entity (LLC/Corp) bulk feeds
County Recorder grant/warranty deed & mortgage recording dockets
Programmatic print-and-mail API (Lob / PostGrid) + QR intake bridge
workflow: Pull daily new-LLC formations (filtering for employer/commercial NAICS or multi-member filings) and newly recorded residential deeds with purchase price and loan metadata
Dispatch transparent, non-governmental trigger mailers within 24–48 hours of filing with personalized QR codes pre-populating entity or parcel data

Monetize new LLCs via recurring annual labor-poster/registered-agent compliance memberships and B2B partner referrals; monetize new deeds via contingency property-tax appeal filings or high-ticket homeowner lead sales
metrics: Filing-to-mailbox latency (hours)
QR scan & intake conversion % per 1,000 mailers
Annualized LTV / net revenue per mailed piece

Ringba / Twilio dynamic number insertion (DNI) & IVR duration billing switch

Partner with a licensed brick-and-mortar operator in each city for legitimate Google Business Profile co-verification while retaining ownership of the domain and tracking numbers

Revenue per qualified call ($75–$300) and contractor retention rate

Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine

Auto-generate uniform comparable-equity evidence packets, file bulk administrative protests before the county bar date, and collect 30–50% of Year-1 tax savings

Percentage of appealed parcels receiving an assessment reduction (65–85% target)
Average net contingency fee per residential ($150–$450) and commercial ($2,000–$15,000) parcel

Title report and statutory redemption calendar
Local counsel priority and notice opinion

4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire

Capital days outstanding
Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate

plays.mechanism: Combine GIS parcel geometry with recorded access rights to option overlooked strips and negotiate voluntary easement assemblages; mapped boundaries alone do not establish legal access.

Surveyor estimates and neighboring-owner demand
workflow: 1. Flag apparently landlocked parcels and narrow connecting strips in GIS

3. Secure contingent options and negotiate voluntary access agreements without obstructing existing access
4. Record approved easements and close the assembled sale through title escrow
metrics: Verified access gaps per screened parcel
Option-to-recorded-easement conversion rate
Net assemblage margin after survey and title costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: GIS false positive or unenforceable access premium
platform_risks.trigger: Unmapped easement, boundary error, or preexisting legal right of access
platform_risks.impact: Option expiry or acquisition with no incremental assemblage value
platform_risks.detection_metric: Survey and title exceptions per shortlisted parcel
platform_risks.fallback: Exercise diligence contingencies and offer survey-backed voluntary access services instead

plays.name: Fractional Heir-Share Acquisition & Tenancy-in-Common Partition Buyout Forcing
plays.mechanism: Acquire documented fractional heir interests at a discount reflecting illiquidity, then seek consensual buyouts or counsel-supervised partition subject to heirs-property protections and co-owner rights.

Title chain, occupancy facts, and independent appraisal
Applicable partition and heirs-property protection rules
workflow: 1. Establish ownership fractions, probate authority, and encumbrances before contacting sellers
2. Provide transparent offers with independent-advice opportunity and modeled partition costs
3. Seek voluntary co-owner buyouts or an agreed market sale before considering litigation
4. If unresolved, use counsel-led statutory procedures honoring notice, appraisal, and buyout rights
metrics: Verified ownership share acquired
Consensual resolution rate
Net proceeds after carrying and legal costs

plays.name: DNS/Script Technographic Drop-Off & Renewal-Window Interception
plays.mechanism: Crawl target commercial domains and DNS TXT/CNAME records weekly to detect the exact day a company installs or removes high-ticket enterprise software tags (Salesforce, HubSpot, Marketo, Segment, NetSuite), predicting annual renewal windows (Month 10–11) and active vendor migrations.
inputs: Weekly HTTP script-tag, DOM header, & DNS TXT/CNAME technographic crawler
Historical install-timestamp ledger (calculating 12-month contract renewal windows)
B2B executive contact graph & migration-agency/SaaS partner routing
workflow: Scan 500,000+ target B2B domains weekly for JavaScript SDKs, tracking pixels, and SPF/CNAME records of $20k–$150k/yr SaaS platforms
Flag accounts entering Month 10 of their annual contract (60 days before auto-renewal lock-in) or accounts running dual competing tags during a live evaluation
Route renewal-window and active-churn signals to competing SaaS sales teams, software resellers, and implementation agencies
metrics: Install/drop detection precision (%) and renewal-date accuracy
Outbound reply-to-demo conversion rate on Month-10 renewal targets
Per-opportunity bounty or retainer revenue per agency/SaaS partner

platform_risks.failure_mode: WAF/Cloudflare bot-blocking or false-positive tag detection from server-side GTM
platform_risks.trigger: High-concurrency crawling from datacenter IPs or misinterpreting server-side tag manager consolidation as vendor churn
platform_risks.impact: Incomplete technographic diffs or wasted sales outreach on false churn signals
platform_risks.detection_metric: Crawler HTTP 200 success rate and multi-signal verification (DNS SPF/CNAME + careers-page job-posting confirmation)
platform_risks.fallback: Combine passive DNS TXT/CNAME monitoring with job-posting technographic mentions to confirm true vendor switches before routing

plays.name: SEC Form 8-K, Form D & C-Suite Turnover Trigger Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Parse SEC EDGAR real-time RSS/JSON feeds for Form D (private Reg D capital raises) and Form 8-K (Item 5.02 C-suite departures, Item 1.01 material agreements, Item 2.01 M&A closings) to trigger sub-hour executive outreach before commercial databases update.
inputs: SEC EDGAR real-time Submissions API & Form D / Form 8-K XML feeds
Automated filing parser extracting raise amounts, executive names, & signatory contacts
Enterprise recruiting, specialty finance, & B2B agency deal-routing desk
workflow: Ingest SEC EDGAR filings within seconds of publication using a compliant User-Agent header (<=10 requests/second)
Extract Form D issuers raising $2M–$50M (who immediately deploy capital on hiring, growth agencies, and software) and Form 8-K executive transitions
Deliver tailored briefings to the filing officers and route warm introductions to executive search firms, enterprise software resellers, and B2B agencies
metrics: EDGAR publication-to-enrichment latency (seconds)
Form D / 8-K executive response rate vs. cold baseline (3–5x lift)
Retainer and placement referral fees generated per 100 filings

platform_risks.impact: Temporary IP block by Akamai/SEC infrastructure

platform_risks.fallback: Enforce token-bucket rate limiting at 5 req/sec and mirror SEC nightly bulk zip archives for historical lookbacks

plays.name: Subsidized / Developer-Tenant Multi-Inbox Cold Outbound Infrastructure
plays.mechanism: Provisioning hundreds of isolated secondary domains across subsidized Microsoft 365 developer/partner tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing, and low-cost SMTP relays—sending strictly 15–25 plain-text emails per inbox per day across 300+ free/subsidized mailboxes to deliver 150,000+ monthly B2B cold emails into primary inboxes without paying $6–$12/seat retail Google Workspace pricing.
inputs: Lookalike secondary domain portfolio with automated SPF, DKIM (2048-bit), DMARC (`p=quarantine`/`reject`), and custom tracking-free MX records
Subsidized M365 partner/developer tenants, Cloudflare Email Routing catch-alls, and distributed SMTP sending nodes
Automated peer-to-peer warmup network and master unibox reply-routing webhook
workflow: Provision 100–300 secondary sending domains and bind 2–3 mailboxes per domain via automated DNS and tenant scripts
Warm every mailbox for 14–21 days with realistic thread-depth conversations before introducing live outbound prospects
Cap daily outbound volume at <=20 zero-link, zero-tracking-pixel plain-text messages per mailbox per day to stay completely beneath ESP volume heuristics
Aggregate all prospect replies into a single unified AI-triaged inbox that books qualified B2B sales calls on pay-per-show or retainer terms
metrics: Primary-inbox placement rate (%) across Gmail and Microsoft 365 seed tests
All-in monthly infrastructure cost per 10,000 delivered plain-text emails ($)
Positive reply rate (%) and booked meetings per 1,000 prospects contacted

plays.name: Employer Self-Funded ERISA Plan International Specialty-Drug Importation Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Contracting with mid-market US employers (100–5,000 employees) operating self-funded ERISA health plans to carve out high-cost specialty biologics and GLP-1s ($6,000–$15,000/mo US PBM list price) and source the identical manufacturer-sealed drugs from licensed Tier-1 pharmacies in Canada, the UK, Australia, and New Zealand at $800–$2,200/mo—waiving the employee's copay to $0 while taking 25–35% of the employer's $50,000–$100,000/yr per-patient savings.
inputs: Department of Labor (DOL) Form 5500 Schedule A/C database identifying self-funded ERISA employers by broker, TPA, and stop-loss carrier
Licensed international pharmacy dispensation network across Tier-1 jurisdictions (Canada, UK, Australia, New Zealand) with cold-chain courier logistics
Turnkey ERISA Summary Plan Description (SPD) 'Specialty Drug Carve-Out Amendment' and $0-copay patient concierge portal
workflow: Mine DOL Form 5500 filings to target CFOs and benefits directors of self-funded companies with 150–3,000 covered lives
Audit the employer's anonymized pharmacy claims file to flag the 1–3% of members driving 45–60% of total drug spend (Humira, Stelara, Skyrizi, Dupixent, Enbrel, Ozempic)
Plug in a voluntary $0-copay international personal-importation program alongside the existing TPA, fulfilling 90-day cold-chain prescriptions at 60–80% below US PBM prices
Bill the self-funded employer plan a shared-savings contingency fee equal to 25–35% of verified net claim reduction ($15,000–$30,000/yr per enrolled specialty patient)
metrics: Verified annual specialty-claim savings ($) per self-funded employer group
Net shared-savings fee revenue ($15k–$30k/yr) per enrolled specialty patient
Employee $0-copay opt-in conversion rate (target: >85%)

platform_risks.fallback: Target independent TPAs and transparent pass-through PBMs first, combine international sourcing with US Manufacturer Patient Assistance Program (PAP) optimization, and maintain domestic bridge-fill coverage

plays.name: 340B Contract-Pharmacy & Covered-Entity Drug Price Spread Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Partnering with HRSA-qualified 340B Covered Entities (Federally Qualified Health Centers, Ryan White clinics, disproportionate-share rural hospitals) to provide turnkey Third-Party Administrator (TPA) split-billing software, specialty contract-pharmacy fulfillment, and tele-referral capture—buying outpatient specialty medications at 25–50%+ statutory 340B discounts while collecting 100% full commercial insurance reimbursement and splitting the multi-thousand-dollar per-script margin via compliant flat administrative/dispensing fees.

340B split-billing / virtual-inventory accumulator software tracking 11-digit NDCs, prescriber NPIs, and patient-eligibility encounters
Licensed specialty/mail-order contract pharmacy network and commercial payer PBMs

Reimburse the pharmacy at full commercial payer rates ($3,000–$12,000/script) while replenishing drug inventory via the clinic's 340B wholesaler account at $800–$4,000/script
Charge fixed fair-market-value per-dispense administrative, software, and clinical-management fees that capture a major share of the net spread while funding the clinic's safety-net mission

Gross commercial-to-340B acquisition spread ($1,500–$6,000+) per specialty fill

platform_risks.impact: Loss of 340B ceiling price on specific NDCs or HRSA repayment liability

platform_risks.fallback: Operate an in-house entity-owned specialty pharmacy location alongside contract pharmacies, automate 340B ESP claims-data uploads to unlock restricted NDCs, and enforce strict EHR encounter gates

plays.name: Section 321 "De Minimis" & Border Bonded-Warehouse Tariff Split-Shipping Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Routing bulk sea/air container imports for high-tariff DTC and marketplace brands into Tijuana (IMMEX) or Canadian border-zone bonded 3PL warehouses instead of US ports, then fulfilling individual US consumer orders across the border daily under 19 U.S.C. § 1321 (Section 321 Entry Type 86)—legally eliminating 15%–42.5% customs duties on qualifying consumer parcels and charging brands 35–50% of the saved tariff bill plus 3PL fulfillment fees.
inputs: USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) database cross-referenced against US Customs Bill-of-Lading import records (ImportYeti / Panjiva / Datamyne)
Nearshore Mexican IMMEX or Canadian customs-bonded fulfillment center 5–15 miles from San Ysidro/Otay Mesa or Windsor/Blaine border crossings
Automated CBP ACE Entry Type 86 manifest software transmitting 10-digit HTS and consignee data per individual consumer parcel
workflow: Scrape public maritime Bill-of-Lading records to identify US apparel, footwear, luggage, and consumer-goods brands importing 20+ containers/yr in 18%–37.5% HTS duty brackets
Divert the client's ocean containers in-bond (IT/T&E bond) directly to the nearshore border-zone fulfillment facility without paying US bulk entry duties
Sync the warehouse WMS with the brand's Shopify/Amazon store so each US consumer order (<$800 retail value, 1 per person per day) is picked, packed, and cleared via CBP Entry Type 86 at $0 duty
Line-item bill the brand for standard pick-and-pack fulfillment plus a 35–50% contingency split of the verified customs duties eliminated
metrics: Annualized customs duty eliminated ($500k–$10M+/yr per enterprise brand client)
Net tariff-savings share + 3PL margin ($) per parcel cleared across the border
CBP Type 86 automated release rate (>99.4%) and border transit time (<6 hours to USPS/FedEx domestic injection)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory exclusion of specific Section 301 country-of-origin SKUs from Section 321 de minimis eligibility
platform_risks.trigger: Executive/statutory rulemaking removing China-origin Section 301 HTS codes from Entry Type 86 eligibility or tightening 10-digit HTS description rules
platform_risks.impact: Loss of Section 321 duty exemption on affected country-of-origin SKUs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Real-time HTS + Country-of-Origin eligibility screen in the WMS before container booking
platform_risks.fallback: Focus on non-301 origin goods (Vietnam, India, EU, Bangladesh, Cambodia) where high MFN duties (16%–32% on apparel/footwear/textiles) remain 100% Section 321 exempt, and pair with CBP First-Sale Valuation for remaining SKUs

plays.name: CBP "First-Sale Rule" (19 CFR § 152.103) Multi-Tier Customs Valuation Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Restructuring multi-tiered import supply chains under the US Court of Appeals *Nissho Iwai* 'First Sale Rule' so US importers legally declare the lower factory-to-middleman transaction price ($8) for US Customs duty and tariff calculation rather than the middleman-to-US-importer invoice price ($18)—slashing annual tariff cash outflows by 35–55% across $10M–$250M+ in imported merchandise.
inputs: US Customs bill-of-lading and HTS duty-spend intelligence identifying mid-market importers paying $1M–$20M/yr in duties via trading companies
Three-party contract, factory cost-sheet, and arm's-length transfer-pricing documentation templates satisfying CBP *Nissho Iwai* criteria
Licensed customs brokerage and trade-attorney opinion pipeline
workflow: Identify US importers purchasing finished goods through Hong Kong, Singapore, Taiwanese, or European trading intermediaries or sourcing agents
Audit the two-tier transaction chain to confirm (1) bona fide sale from factory to middleman, (2) clear designation for US export at factory order, and (3) arm's-length pricing
Implement compliant multi-tier invoicing and ERP documentary trails so the customs broker declares the factory's First-Sale price on CBP Form 7501 instead of the middleman's marked-up invoice
Collect a 25–35% contingency fee on all prospective and retroactive (Post-Summary Correction / Protest) duty reductions realized by the importer
metrics: Percentage reduction in declared customs dutiable value (typically 30–50%)
Annualized cash tariff savings ($300k–$5M+/yr per importer) and retroactive PSC refund recovery ($)
CBP CF-28/CF-29 Request for Information audit survival rate (100% documentary compliance)

platform_risks.impact: Re-assessment of duties on the second-sale price plus interest
platform_risks.detection_metric: Annual pre-audit verification of factory commercial invoices, bank wire proofs, and OECD transfer-pricing benchmark studies
platform_risks.fallback: Store encrypted factory invoices in a confidential customs-broker escrow vault (so the US buyer never sees the middleman's margin, while CBP auditors have full access) and back every program with a formal customs-counsel opinion letter

plays.name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Price small HOA priority liens and tax-sale interests using jurisdiction-specific priority, notice, and redemption rules; returns depend on enforceable rights, not assumed title extinguishment.
inputs: County tax-sale and HOA lien records
Title report and statutory redemption calendar
Local counsel priority and notice opinion
workflow: 1. Screen small-balance liens against property value, senior debt, and sale eligibility
2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions
3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline
4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire
metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs
Capital days outstanding
Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien
platform_risks.trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority
platform_risks.impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition
platform_risks.fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests

plays.name: Fractional Heir-Share Acquisition & Tenancy-in-Common Partition Buyout Forcing
plays.mechanism: Acquire documented fractional heir interests at a discount reflecting illiquidity, then seek consensual buyouts or counsel-supervised partition subject to heirs-property protections and co-owner rights.
inputs: Probate files and verified heirship records
Title chain, occupancy facts, and independent appraisal
Applicable partition and heirs-property protection rules
workflow: 1. Establish ownership fractions, probate authority, and encumbrances before contacting sellers
2. Provide transparent offers with independent-advice opportunity and modeled partition costs
3. Seek voluntary co-owner buyouts or an agreed market sale before considering litigation
4. If unresolved, use counsel-led statutory procedures honoring notice, appraisal, and buyout rights
metrics: Verified ownership share acquired
Consensual resolution rate
Net proceeds after carrying and legal costs

platform_risks.failure_mode: Heirs-property protections defeat assumed forced-sale economics
platform_risks.trigger: Mandatory co-owner buyout, partition-in-kind preference, or defective heirship
platform_risks.impact: Long holding period and lower realizable value
platform_risks.detection_metric: Unresolved heirs and statutory buyout conditions per property
platform_risks.fallback: Renegotiate voluntary exits or retain the interest without threatening unavailable remedies

plays.name: Whitelisted Agency Ad-Spend Card-Multiplier Points & Volume-Rebate Cycling
plays.mechanism: Route genuine client-authorized advertising spend through eligible agency payment arrangements to earn contract-permitted rewards and volume rebates, net of financing, processing, and client pass-through obligations.
inputs: Client media mandates and rebate ownership clauses
Issuer reward categories, caps, and repayment terms
Platform invoices and agency volume-rebate agreements
workflow: 1. Verify client authorization, platform payment permissions, and ownership of rewards and rebates
2. Model eligible media purchases against reward caps, fees, liquidity, and rebate thresholds
3. Pay only genuine approved advertising invoices without circular spend or fabricated transactions
4. Reconcile settled rewards, client credits, refunds, and full card repayment each statement cycle
metrics: Net retained rewards and rebates per media dollar
Unfunded client exposure and repayment coverage
Invoice-to-reward reconciliation variance

platform_risks.failure_mode: Reward clawback or client-funded liquidity shortfall
platform_risks.trigger: Ineligible categories, prohibited payment aggregation, or delayed client reimbursement
platform_risks.impact: Lost rebates, interest costs, and card suspension
platform_risks.detection_metric: Denied reward value and overdue client balances versus cash reserves
platform_risks.fallback: Move to client-direct billing or prefunded approved agency terms and stop rewards-dependent spending

plays.name: TCPA Serial-Plaintiff Docket Scraping & Real-Time Litigator-Scrub Firewall Tollbooth
plays.mechanism: Offer consent-first outbound compliance screening using lawful docket-derived risk signals alongside mandatory do-not-call and revocation checks; plaintiff matching neither authorizes contact nor replaces TCPA compliance.
inputs: Permitted public docket data with identity confidence scores
Consent provenance, revocations, and suppression lists
Applicable calling rules and customer retention policies
workflow: 1. Ingest permitted docket records with source dates, minimization, and human identity review
2. Check consent, do-not-call status, revocations, and calling restrictions before optional risk enrichment
3. Suppress noncompliant contacts and route uncertain matches to review without planting honeypots or provoking claims
4. Serve auditable screening decisions with correction, deletion, and retention controls
metrics: Contacts blocked for missing consent or suppression match
False-positive identity match rate
Screening latency and stale-record share

platform_risks.failure_mode: False identity match or false assurance of permission to call
platform_risks.trigger: Stale docket data or treating absence from a plaintiff list as consent
platform_risks.impact: Unlawful outreach, privacy complaints, and customer liability
platform_risks.detection_metric: Consent-audit failure rate and upheld identity correction requests
platform_risks.fallback: Disable uncertain enrichment and require independently verified consent and authoritative suppression checks

plays.name: New-LLC & Recorded-Deed Trigger-Mail Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Ingest daily Secretary of State new-LLC filings and County Recorder new-deed/mortgage recordings to trigger programmatic direct mail via API—replacing illegal government-lookalike poster/deed invoices (which violate 39 U.S.C. § 3001 and state deed-solicitation laws) with high-LTV recurring workplace compliance subscriptions, property-tax appeal contingency offers, and exclusive new-mover/B2B lead monetization.
inputs: Daily Secretary of State new-entity (LLC/Corp) bulk feeds
County Recorder grant/warranty deed & mortgage recording dockets
Programmatic print-and-mail API (Lob / PostGrid) + QR intake bridge
workflow: Pull daily new-LLC formations (filtering for employer/commercial NAICS or multi-member filings) and newly recorded residential deeds with purchase price and loan metadata
Dispatch transparent, non-governmental trigger mailers within 24–48 hours of filing with personalized QR codes pre-populating entity or parcel data

Monetize new LLCs via recurring annual labor-poster/registered-agent compliance memberships and B2B partner referrals; monetize new deeds via contingency property-tax appeal filings or high-ticket homeowner lead sales
metrics: Filing-to-mailbox latency (hours)
QR scan & intake conversion % per 1,000 mailers
Annualized LTV / net revenue per mailed piece

platform_risks.failure_mode: USPS 39 U.S.C. § 3001(h)-(i) mail-stop order, State AG UDAP enforcement, or payment-processor freeze

platform_risks.impact: Civil restitution penalties, merchant account termination, and 30%+ chargeback rates
platform_risks.detection_metric: Refund/chargeback ratio >1% and customer support inquiries mistaking the mailer for a government agency
platform_risks.fallback: Use unambiguous private commercial branding, never mimic government seals or citation numbers, and sell genuine value-add subscriptions (annual compliance updates, tax-assessment appeals, or B2B services)

Self-serve $299–$799/mo Featured Placement & exclusive lead-routing checkout

Notify top-scoring firms with their free embeddable HTML/SVG '2026 Top-Scored Provider' badge (driving natural dofollow backlinks back to your directory)

plays.name: Automated Parcel, LTL Freight & Tariff Overcharge Contingency Auditing
plays.mechanism: Ingest mid-market shippers' UPS/FedEx/LTL EDI billing feeds and CBP Form 7501 customs entry summaries via read-only API to programmatically flag late-delivery SLA refunds, dimensional-weight billing errors, and duty-drawback refunds on a 35–50% contingency split.
inputs: Read-only UPS/FedEx/LTL carrier billing API & EDI 210 feeds
CBP ACE Form 7501 customs entry & HTS tariff schedules
Automated carrier dispute & duty-drawback claim submission engine
workflow: Connect read-only to shipper parcel/freight portals and ingest historical and daily invoice line items
Flag guaranteed-service late deliveries, duplicate accessorial fees, residential surcharges, and eligible export duty drawbacks
Auto-file carrier credit disputes and customs drawback claims, billing the client strictly 35–50% of verified credits posted to their statement
metrics: Recovered credits as % of total annual parcel/freight spend (2–8% target)
Dispute acceptance rate by carrier/customs (%)
Monthly recurring contingency revenue per shipper account

platform_risks.failure_mode: Carrier anti-automation lockouts or GSR (Guaranteed Service Refund) waiver clauses

platform_risks.fallback: Pivot audit rules toward non-waivable dimensional-weight, duplicate-charge, LTL freight class, and contract-rate benchmarking recoveries

plays.name: FMCSA/DOT New-Authority & Roadside Violation Trigger Funnels
plays.mechanism: Ingest daily federal FMCSA Census, Licensing & Insurance (L&I), and SMS roadside-inspection violation feeds to intercept newly granted MC/DOT authorities (during the mandatory 21-day insurance-filing window) and fleets with fresh HOS/maintenance citations.
inputs: FMCSA daily Licensing & Insurance (L&I) pending-authority feed
FMCSA Safety Measurement System (SMS) roadside violation & BASIC score logs
Commercial trucking insurance, factoring, & ELD compliance partner network
workflow: Poll daily FMCSA pending-application feeds to identify carriers that received a docket number but still need BOC-3 and BIPD insurance filings to go active
Monitor SMS inspection logs for fleets cited for ELD, hours-of-service, or maintenance violations requiring corrective action plans
Route carriers in real time to commercial truck insurance brokers ($500–$1,500 CPA/split), freight factoring desks, and compliance consultants
metrics: FMCSA filing-to-contact latency (minutes)
Pending-authority to bound-policy conversion %
Combined CPA from insurance, BOC-3, ELD, and factoring referrals

plays.name: Section 321 "De Minimis" & Border Bonded-Warehouse Tariff Split-Shipping Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Routing bulk sea/air container imports for high-tariff DTC and marketplace brands into Tijuana (IMMEX) or Canadian border-zone bonded 3PL warehouses instead of US ports, then fulfilling individual US consumer orders across the border daily under 19 U.S.C. § 1321 (Section 321 Entry Type 86)—legally eliminating 15%–42.5% customs duties on qualifying consumer parcels and charging brands 35–50% of the saved tariff bill plus 3PL fulfillment fees.
inputs: USITC Harmonized Tariff Schedule (HTS) database cross-referenced against US Customs Bill-of-Lading import records (ImportYeti / Panjiva / Datamyne)
Nearshore Mexican IMMEX or Canadian customs-bonded fulfillment center 5–15 miles from San Ysidro/Otay Mesa or Windsor/Blaine border crossings
Automated CBP ACE Entry Type 86 manifest software transmitting 10-digit HTS and consignee data per individual consumer parcel
workflow: Scrape public maritime Bill-of-Lading records to identify US apparel, footwear, luggage, and consumer-goods brands importing 20+ containers/yr in 18%–37.5% HTS duty brackets
Divert the client's ocean containers in-bond (IT/T&E bond) directly to the nearshore border-zone fulfillment facility without paying US bulk entry duties
Sync the warehouse WMS with the brand's Shopify/Amazon store so each US consumer order (<$800 retail value, 1 per person per day) is picked, packed, and cleared via CBP Entry Type 86 at $0 duty
Line-item bill the brand for standard pick-and-pack fulfillment plus a 35–50% contingency split of the verified customs duties eliminated
metrics: Annualized customs duty eliminated ($500k–$10M+/yr per enterprise brand client)
Net tariff-savings share + 3PL margin ($) per parcel cleared across the border
CBP Type 86 automated release rate (>99.4%) and border transit time (<6 hours to USPS/FedEx domestic injection)

platform_risks.failure_mode: Statutory exclusion of specific Section 301 country-of-origin SKUs from Section 321 de minimis eligibility
platform_risks.trigger: Executive/statutory rulemaking removing China-origin Section 301 HTS codes from Entry Type 86 eligibility or tightening 10-digit HTS description rules
platform_risks.impact: Loss of Section 321 duty exemption on affected country-of-origin SKUs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Real-time HTS + Country-of-Origin eligibility screen in the WMS before container booking
platform_risks.fallback: Focus on non-301 origin goods (Vietnam, India, EU, Bangladesh, Cambodia) where high MFN duties (16%–32% on apparel/footwear/textiles) remain 100% Section 321 exempt, and pair with CBP First-Sale Valuation for remaining SKUs

plays.name: Authorized-Distributor "Diversion" & Grey-Market Luxury / Medical Consumables Arbitrage
plays.mechanism: Exploiting multinational manufacturers' 35–60% regional price discrimination by using foreign corporate purchasing entities to buy container-loads of 100% authentic branded goods (luxury fragrances, prestige cosmetics, Swiss watches, OTC diabetic test strips, salon haircare, OEM imaging supplies) from over-quota authorized distributors in emerging/EMEA/LATAM markets and importing them into US off-price retail (TJX, Costco, Burlington) and Amazon wholesale channels under the Supreme Court's First-Sale Doctrine (*Kirtsaeng v. John Wiley & Sons*).
inputs: Global wholesale price-book matrix comparing US net distributor pricing against EMEA, LATAM, Eastern European, and Asian-Pacific tier-1 distributor net pricing
Foreign purchasing subsidiaries (UAE, Poland, Panama, Singapore, Cyprus) with clean trade references and escrow inspection facilities
SGS/Bureau Veritas pre-shipment authenticity verification and batch-code sanitization SOPs
workflow: Identify authentic global SKUs with >40% wholesale price spreads between emerging-market distributor books and US off-price wholesale demand
Approach regional authorized distributors near end-of-quarter who need to move $500k–$5M in excess allocation to hit their manufacturer volume-tier rebate
Purchase the sealed master cases via a foreign trading entity, conduct third-party SGS lot authentication, and remove secondary distributor tracking labels that could identify the source distributor
Import the goods legally under First-Sale exhaustion and flip on back-to-back POs to US off-price retail chains, pharmacy wholesalers, and verified marketplace aggregators
metrics: Gross landed price spread (22–45% net margin) between foreign distributor cost and US wholesale PO price
Inventory cash-conversion cycle (days from escrow release to US buyer wire settlement)
100% lot-level manufacturer authenticity verification and chain-of-custody pass rate

platform_risks.failure_mode: Brand-owner Lanham Act 'material difference' trademark challenge or marketplace invoice rejection
platform_risks.trigger: Importing foreign-language packaging or altered warranty/formulation SKUs that differ materially from the US domestic version
platform_risks.impact: CBP detention or Amazon brand-gating suppression on specific ASINs
platform_risks.detection_metric: Pre-purchase SKU inspection confirming identical UPC/EAN, multi-language compliant labeling, and identical physical formulation
